findings.title: Table public.orders is readable by anyone: row-level security is off
findings.impact: Anyone who opens the shop can download every customer's orders and addresses with the public key shipped in the page.
findings.evidence: pg_tables.rowsecurity = false for public.orders; role anon holds SELECT.
findings.fix: ALTER TABLE public.orders ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; add a policy USING (auth.uid() = customer_id). Rollback: DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
findings.verify: Re-run the pg_tables query, then request the table with the public key: it must return only the caller's rows.

findings.title: Order lookup trusts the ID in the URL (missing ownership check)
findings.impact: A logged-in customer can read another customer's order by changing the number in the address bar.
findings.evidence: src/routes/orders.ts:42 loads the order by req.params.id without comparing it to the session user.
findings.fix: Filter the query by the session's customer id and return 404 when it does not match.
findings.verify: Request another account's order id: expect 404. Add a regression test.

findings.title: Check dependencies automatically on every pull request
findings.evidence: No dependency scan in the CI workflow.
findings.fix: Add a lockfile scan (for example osv-scanner) to CI and fail the build on new high-severity advisories.

findings.title: Add rate limiting to login and password reset
findings.evidence: No rate limit observed in the gateway configuration.
findings.fix: Limit attempts per account and per address, and alert on bursts.
